description: The Obsidian MCP server that needs no plugin, no running Obsidian app — and doesn't blow your context window. Filesystem-direct: single-digit-ms keyword search, ~26 ms local semantic search, ~2 KB payloads, 25 tools.

tool_signatures.name: Local semantic search, fully in-process. With SEEKSTONE_SEMANTIC=1, search and context_pack gain mode
tool_signatures.description: "semantic" and "hybrid" — meaning-based retrieval through a small on-device embedding model (one-time npx -y seekstone fetch-model download, or the seekstone-semantic.mcpb bundle which ships the model inside; the running server never touches the network), with a MaxSim late-interaction rerank on top since 0.17.0. On our committed 10k-note benchmark vault (150-query golden set, fixture v2), the default model — measured end-to-end through the real search tool — scores 83.3% overall hit@5, 86.7% on the held-out split (vs 34.7% for keyword search alone) at ~26 ms warm p50, and the opt-in potion-retrieval-32M model (SEEKSTONE_SEMANTIC_MODEL; ~129 MB) reaches 86.7% overall hit@5, 86.7% held-out at ~55 ms. No other server we benchmarked ships offline, zero-native-dependency embeddings — and we measured the alternatives head-to-head on the same golden set, same run, committed dev/holdout split ([committed comparison](packages/harness/fixtures/baseline-reports/retrieval-eval-competitors.md), read-out in [COMPETITORS-SHA-322](packages/harness/fixtures/baseline-reports/COMPETITORS-SHA-322.md)): obsidian-tc's plain Ollama-backed semantic search edges us on the held-out split (90.0% vs our 86.7%) at 169 ms/query and a 30-minute index vs our ~28 s, and its GraphRAG mode scores highest of anything we benchmarked (95.0% held-out), paying for it with seconds-per-query latency (2.9 s p50, 4.2 s p95 — against our 26–55 ms), ~8× the payload (16 KB vs ~2 KB per query), and a second server (Ollama + a 137M-parameter model) you must install and run. We pre-registered a gate to claim the #1 spot ([GATE-V2-SHA-316](packages/harness/fixtures/baseline-reports/GATE-V2-SHA-316.md), run on fixture v1) and missed it — that verdict is published with the same prominence a win would have been; no new gate ran on v2, and the same clauses recompute to the same miss. obsidian-mcp-pro could not index the 10k-note vault at all (its JSON vector store exceeds JavaScript's string limit after ~17 minutes of embedding). Pick your trade — the numbers are all committed.

tool_signatures.name: append_note
tool_signatures.description: Append text to a note body without touching frontmatter.

tool_signatures.name: append_periodic_note
tool_signatures.description: Append to today's periodic note, creating it from a template if it doesn't yet exist.

tool_signatures.name: context_pack
tool_signatures.description: Answer-ready context for a natural-language question in one call, hard-capped at a byte budget (default 2 KB): ranked excerpts, linked neighbor notes with one-line summaries, and follow-up source paths — replaces a search → read → get_backlinks round-trip loop. Scopable by folder/tag and takes the same mode as search.

tool_signatures.name: create_note
tool_signatures.description: Create a note (optional frontmatter + body); parent directories are created automatically.

tool_signatures.name: delete_note
tool_signatures.description: Move a note to the vault's .trash/ folder (Obsidian-compatible, restorable). Pass permanent: true to skip the trash — the write journal still lets undo_write restore it.

tool_signatures.name: get_backlinks
tool_signatures.description: Find all notes that link to a given note.

tool_signatures.name: get_links
tool_signatures.description: List all outgoing wikilinks and markdown links from a note.

tool_signatures.name: get_periodic_note
tool_signatures.description: Read today's (or any date's) daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, or yearly note — path resolved from your vault config, no Obsidian required.

tool_signatures.name: list_notes
tool_signatures.description: List notes, optionally filtered by folder prefix or tag.

tool_signatures.name: list_tags
tool_signatures.description: List all tags in the vault sorted by usage count (or alphabetically).

tool_signatures.name: list_tasks
tool_signatures.description: List Markdown checkbox tasks as compact structured rows (path, line, state, text, nearest heading) — vault-wide or filtered by note, folder, tag, state, or modified time. Custom markers (- [/], - [-], …) are first-class single-char states.

tool_signatures.name: list_writes
tool_signatures.description: Recent writes from the journal — seq, timestamp, tool, touched paths, and whether each is still undoable. Metadata only, never note content.

tool_signatures.name: move_note
tool_signatures.description: Move or rename a note — wikilinks and markdown links in other notes that point at it are rewritten so nothing breaks (rewriteLinks: false to opt out); destination directories are created automatically.

tool_signatures.name: outline_note
tool_signatures.description: Return a note's heading and block structure without its full content — cheap navigation before a targeted read.

tool_signatures.name: patch_frontmatter
tool_signatures.description: Set, update, or delete frontmatter keys without reordering existing keys or changing quote style.

tool_signatures.name: patch_note
tool_signatures.description: Append, prepend, or replace text at a heading or block reference (createIfMissing to add the section) — frontmatter untouched.

tool_signatures.name: query_notes
tool_signatures.description: Structured metadata query. Filter by frontmatter key/value predicates (eq, ne, contains, exists, missing, gt/gte/lt/lte), tag, folder, modified time, and size; sort and select the fields you need. Returns compact rows (path + title by default), not note content.

tool_signatures.name: read_note
tool_signatures.description: Read the full content of a note by vault-relative path. Supports returning a single section, block, or line range.

tool_signatures.name: read_notes
tool_signatures.description: Read up to 20 notes (or sections, blocks, line ranges) in one call under a total byte budget (default 16 KB). Over budget, each note is cut to a fair share and marked truncated; one bad path returns its own error without failing the batch.

tool_signatures.name: rename_heading
tool_signatures.description: Rename a heading in a note — every [[note#heading]] wikilink and embed across the vault is rewritten so references keep working (aliases preserved, fenced code blocks left alone).

tool_signatures.name: replace_in_note
tool_signatures.description: Find and replace text in the note body — literal or regex, case sensitivity, whole-word matching, optional limit (replaces all occurrences by default), and a dry-run preview.

tool_signatures.name: resolve_note
tool_signatures.description: Turn a note name, path, or frontmatter alias into its canonical vault path(s) — with provenance per match, all candidates when ambiguous, and did-you-mean suggestions when nothing matches.

tool_signatures.name: search
tool_signatures.description: Full-text search. Returns ranked excerpts (default ~120 chars, tunable via excerptLength), not full notes. Fuzzy and prefix matching; with SEEKSTONE_SEMANTIC=1, mode: "semantic"/"hybrid" searches by meaning via a local embedding model (nothing leaves your machine).

tool_signatures.name: undo_write
tool_signatures.description: Revert a journaled write: every file it touched goes back to its byte-identical pre-write state (a multi-file move or heading rename is restored whole; a delete is restored even if it was permanent). Defaults to the most recent write; refuses with undo_conflict if a file changed since, unless force: true. The undo is itself journaled — undo_write({ seq }) on the undo entry redoes it.

tool_signatures.name: update_task
tool_signatures.description: Set one checkbox's state by path + line (from list_tasks) — rewrites exactly one character, leaving every other byte untouched. An expectText guard refuses if the task text changed since it was listed.
